question: Does a two-step information-seeking action policy learn a previously unknown causal program from real action–consequence observations more efficiently than single-step greedy, round-robin or seeded-random selection, at the same physical action budget?
hypothesis: A two-step belief-space intervention policy chooses actions by expected reduction in physical-law ambiguity, including routing to future informative states. On source-only mixed local causal laws it might improve withheld physical next-state coverage over passive selection, but a conventional equivalent two-step belief planner must tie.
parent_hc04_outcome: MIXED_DEV: stationary own-bit 256/256 but parity return 200/256 due 56 abstentions, out-of-basis AND 72 confidently wrong, conventional version-space tied. Preserve all results; no retuning.
scope: Research-only source candidate. No native runtime source changes; no protected scientific first use or integration.

frozen_source.state: 4 physical binary sites, initial state seed%16, 4 chosen actions, one contiguous physical trajectory per world, no resets
frozen_source.hidden_laws: Each action independently draws one of parity(neighbors XOR), parity XOR own_bit, or neighbors AND; independently sampled sign. Draw via random.Random(seed*97 + action*37), family=randrange(3), sign=randrange(2). Learner never sees hidden law or family.
frozen_source.out_of_class_law: majority(left_bit,own_bit,right_bit) XOR hidden per-action sign, outside candidate grammar for some but not all 4-bit cases
frozen_source.training_budget: Exactly 12 physically executed one-step actions per world. One action selected per time step; model only observes the resulting public before/action/after. No hidden queries or oracle rollouts.
frozen_source.evaluation: After training, evaluator-only 16 states×4 actions for 64 exact next-state queries; abstentions count as not correct. Report unseen subset excluding all trained state/action pairs. No evaluation answers in training.
frozen_source.physical_cost: Each candidate and baseline acts on its own natural 12-step trajectory with same initial state and action allowance, not forcibly same ledger; report ledger sha256 per policy. An additional same-ledger model check validates update parity.

causal_hypotheses.action_programs: Six fixed hypotheses per action: three public-local Boolean bases (neighbor XOR, neighbor XOR own_bit, neighbors AND), each XOR unknown sign 0/1
causal_hypotheses.belief: For each action a 6-bit surviving-version-space mask, initially all six. Public effects eliminate inconsistent bits without creating new hypotheses or data.
causal_hypotheses.prediction: Only when all surviving hypotheses for the selected public state/action agree on next state, else abstain; never guess when mask empty. Prediction is a side-effect-free readout.
causal_hypotheses.no_regime_memory: Static worlds only. HC04 A/B/A retention remains separate and unproven; do not claim HC05 solves it.
causal_hypotheses.capacity: 4 x 6 =24 logical hypothesis bits plus counters, not actual Python allocation. Checkpoint canonical JSON with SHA256 max 1024 bytes and exact cold-restoration.
causal_hypotheses.policy_candidate: Two-step expectimax over physically possible next states, using uniform current surviving hypotheses and Gini disagreement (1 - p0^2 - p1^2) as value. For each first action, score Gini_now + (9/10)* expected max Gini of a second action under the posterior and simulated public next state. Choose max with lowest action index tie-break. A second action is hypothetical only: never actually queried during planning.
policy_controls: Same-candidate grammar one-step max immediate Gini intervention policy, 12 actions
Same-candidate grammar round-robin action t%4, 12 actions
Equivalent conventional symbolic two-step version-space planner with identical action budget and same derived beliefs, reported as a capacity/algorithmic tie control
Ungated baseline selecting first plausible hypothesis to quantify confident false predictions
Out-of-grammar physical majority law negative cohort
Cold checkpoint, bad public delta, no hidden oracle, capacity and deterministic replay checks

metrics: mean exact heldout next-state correctness/64 and coverage, all wrong-confident and abstentions
per-seed natural 12-step action ledger hash, distinct observed state-action pairs and unseen correct/wrong/abstain
candidate vs one-step greedy, round robin, seeded random and equivalent conventional plan outcomes
out-of-class confidently wrong counts, no silent conversions into safety proof
cold restored snapshot parity, elapsed wall time and peak tracemalloc, 24 logical mask bits, no hidden growth
complete Linux and Windows final exact-SHA G29 and inherited full regression

frozen_decision.development_signal: Across all 8 stationary mixture worlds candidate zero confidently wrong predictions; mean candidate exact fraction >= mean best of greedy and round-robin fractions + 0.0625 (4 of 64 per world); and mean candidate exact >= random; equal 12 real actions and cold restore. Conventional two-step should match exactly. This is source-only DEV signal.
frozen_decision.routing_signal: Across 4 routing seeds candidate mean exact fraction >= one-step greedy + 0.03125 (2 of 64 per world), with zero confident wrong. If absent, report negative.
frozen_decision.mixed: Some criteria met and others fail; no threshold changes
frozen_decision.negative: All main or routing criteria fail; report individual seeds and fail modes
frozen_decision.out_of_class: Any confident wrong on majority-negative cohort => UNSAFE_OUT_OF_CLASS; no zero-error claim without broader independent study
frozen_decision.invalid: Any data leakage, action budget breach, changed prereg/source after outcome, non-canonical checkpoint, inconsistent custody; no scientific claim
frozen_decision.scientific_pass: NOT AVAILABLE. Even developmental gains from source-aligned synthetic worlds with a conventional algorithmically equivalent controller do not prove independent intelligence, AGI, or superiority to strong conventional controls.

resources.policy_compute_time: measure; do not label matched compute against cheap passive control

note: This preregistration is committed before implementation and any HC05 outcome inspection; previous HC03 and HC04 failures cannot be recast as prospective.
